description: The Clawdbot-era macOS app, installed for real, so the predecessor bundle id is a fact rather than a zap-stanza transcription.
why: bot.molt.mac and bot.molt. were carried as aliases for a release that never shipped -- the app has only ever been Clawdis, Clawdbot and OpenClaw across 243 releases. This scenario installs the real predecessor so its identifier can enter the catalog the way every other one does. `must_find` is EMPTY and `openclaw` is FORBIDDEN deliberately: com.clawdbot.mac is not in the catalog yet, so the classifier must not claim OpenClaw from this app, and asserting that is what proves the raw probe below is testing the row rather than a signature that already exists. The catalog entry and the must_find land once a CI run has produced the row -- this pull request's own run will do, with the row committed under test/fixtures/captured/ to carry the coverage gate. An identifier enters when a run produced it, not when a maintainer read it off a dmg.
known_gaps: The bundle id only. com.clawdbot. as a launchd prefix is NOT asserted: the binary contains com.clawdbot.gateway, but a LaunchAgent is registered when the app RUNS, and this scenario only installs. Whether an unlaunched install produces a daemon row is unverified, which is why the prefix is not in the catalog either.
Clawdis, the generation before this one, ships its own macOS app and is not covered. Its bundle id has not been read off the artifact, so nothing is claimed about it.
